note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of discordant imaging and negative biopsy findings to determine the necessity of further diagnostic intervention or initiation of active surveillance.

Recently retired retired carpenter with a history of mildly elevated PSA levels over the past three years, currently measuring 0.76 ng/mL. He reports no lower urinary tract symptoms, with an IPSS score of 5/35, and denies any haematuria, dysuria, or nocturia. He is married, lives with his partner, and remains socially active, engaging in swimming once a week. He quit smoking in 2010 after a 21 pack-year history and consumes approximately 2 units of alcohol per week. Recent appointments include an audiology hearing test, a routine dental check-up, and a flu vaccination administered by the practice nurse. He has no recorded comorbidities and takes no regular medications. He prefers morning appointments due to reliance on public transport.

On DRE, the prostate is non-palpable, consistent with a clinical T stage of cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished man with stable vital signs, including a blood pressure of 136/69 mmHg and a heart rate of 74 bpm. There is no peripheral lymphadenopathy or signs of bone tenderness.
